thesis: Water-surface geometry (slope + within-overpass heterogeneity) is a stronger indicator than water area; extent-based fragmentation contrasts are coverage-confounded.

thesis: SWOT and ICESat-2 agree at the cm level only under close temporal collocation; the fast-sampling calibration orbit recorded the outlet drawdown and the flood wave below the dam, and the 2023 surge is recorded by the estuary posts.
Cross-sensor interpretation requires explicit vertical-reference harmonisation: one EPSG:9902 grid, EGG2015, permanent tide handled, station correctors that do not transfer.

Legacy soundings and design documentation constrain both ends: the 1970 free surface bounds pre-breach slopes; the bed reconstruction (ZONE_1 hist14; ZONE_2/3/4 p28 soundings-only) reproduces the historical drawdown exposure within a datum band; shoreline-contour constraints do not help.
publication_readiness: P0: update exposure numbers, regenerate V12/V13/V15, propagate datum band

thesis: The slope–discharge relationship after the breach is NOT TESTABLE (no 2024–2025 discharge overlap).

The seamless terrain delivered to the companion paper is validated by two independent lidars (ICESat-2 night returns and GEDI ground returns), and that validation also exposes a seam defect which must be repaired before the terrain carries a hydraulic model.
publication_readiness: blocked by B8.2 (seam defect, 30.8 km2 at -21.75 m vs FABDEM); everything else ready

thesis: The exposed bed revegetated within two seasons (27 → 72 → 84 % of the former water surface), with reed peaking in 2024 and woody cover emerging by 2024–2025; ICESat-2 gives canopy-height distributions but no change.
publication_readiness: ready as area/transition series; no accuracy statement (T27)

thesis: The channel below the dam is wider after the breach at matched stage (+~100 m, main arm 500 → 560 m) with transient braiding in June 2023.

Translated through literature priors, the mapped surface classes of the former pool imply roughly twice the area-weighted flow resistance by 2025 (a derived roughness layer, not a calibrated Manning coefficient); the floodway also roughens; no hydraulic calibration exists.
Over freshly exposed sediment an anchored single-date SAR discriminant is the usable baseline; change detection fails recall; false water is land-cover conditioned and needs a rejection stage.
publication_readiness: supplement_only / future RS paper — methods and negative results
